Audited game-server subset from [Boi-027/overwatch-1.74-lobby-server](https://github.com/Boi-027/overwatch-1.74-lobby-server/tree/0fa61b950dfc9c915cb2353d2873d6d4689c2a5e), MIT license, pinned commit `0fa61b950dfc9c915cb2353d2873d6d4689c2a5e`.

Imported game transport, world replication, input decoding, hero selection, statescript serialization, JAM codec and their two JSON data files (`game_maps_174.json` added 2026-11-02 from the same commit). Lobby schemas retain the handoff group, plus (added 2026-11-03 from the same commit) the hero catalog `0x70E5A247`, progression `0x779A8581`, party `0x2411DE56` and config `0x1732EBF2` groups, the events group `0x8B77C823` the gallery group `0xB68870B8`, and the social-out `0x75D32AE2` and lobby `0x1A9879A4` groups and (2026-11-05, same commit) the queue groups `0x1C6EC712`, `0xB4F8BC62` and `0xA1498A6A` and the Arcade group `0x00A8654E`; `data/arcade_174.json` holds that commit's `arcade_cards_174.json` (the 0x063 mode cards) and the recorded 39802's Quick Play and competitive cards. `data/resource_keys_174.json` (content key name and bytes per key asset, 189 entries) is copied unchanged from the same commit. `ow174/paths.py` points to adjacent data. Local server changes ensure exclusive port ownership, close failed binds/thread starts, join the server thread on shutdown and log inbound message IDs without decoded names. Empty package initializers are local.

No upstream launcher, dashboard, relay, authentication service or executable patches are included. Requires the already-installed `cryptography` package. This snapshot does not implement authoritative weapon/ability simulation; its remote-player mover has no collision, gravity or jumping. Local client prediction requires separate runtime verification.

Local input diagnostics record throttle/button changes (no text or account fields) to distinguish missing input from missing simulation. The launcher checks lobby liveness throughout each bounded session.

Soldier body creation now schedules the local held-rifle frame after two seconds and acknowledges delivered body states with the existing command-frame protocol. A new hero pick resets this state. Body initialization lives in adjacent `tools/lobby/soldier.py`.

An explicit `gameplay` gate adds command-driven rifle updates and the original Training Bot fixture; it defaults false in the vendor Match and GameServer. The owned Practice Range server enables it and supplies the verified Soldier body setup from `soldier.py`. Research BodyProbeServer skips that setup to preserve isolated phases. Normal session210119 verifies the HUD, ten-shot target removal/respawn and manual reload. Fixture physics uses server flat movement and a sphere without map occlusion; this is not a complete original gameplay simulation.

`match.py` / `server.py` (2026-11-05): `LOADING_GATES` and `Match.pre_load_updates` send a scripted-loading mode's graph with its marker state before the map loads; normal modes are unchanged. An experiment, see `tools/lobby/CHANGELOG.md`.

2026-11-08: added an optional `on_finish` notification from Assault completion to the local lobby, defaulting to `None` in the vendor server/Match. Retained progression-out group `7F4F46CB` messages 24200–24203 from the pinned schema for native inventory/open/report/purchase requests. Account persistence, reward policy and request validation remain in adjacent local modules; no upstream profile/reset code was imported.

2026-11-09: added the statescript decoder from [LizRollin/overwatch-1.74-lobby-server](https://github.com/LizRollin/overwatch-1.74-lobby-server/tree/9f8f3bcb5eccab6fb7738bee3c2371fcf0623f29), pinned commit `9f8f3bcb5eccab6fb7738bee3c2371fcf0623f29`, under the same MIT license and copyright notice as `LICENSE`. Copied byte for byte: `ow174/game/script/{__init__,codecs,decode,expr,graph}.py`, `data/statescript_codecs_174.json` (the client's codec table) and `data/game_graphs_174.json.gz` (373-graph catalog). The game server does not import them. They serve the test oracle `tools/lobby/oracle.py` only. Evaluation: research/lizrollin-runtime.md.

2026-11-09: the player's mover is LizRollin's port of the client's mover, at the same pin and license as above. Copied byte for byte: `ow174/game/{mover,contacts,collision,casc,props}.py` (`mover.py` replaces the snapshot's flat mover) and `data/{game_movers_174,collision_props_174,collision_keys_174}.json`. `casc.py` only reads the installed game's archives. Local change: `ow174/paths.py` adds `ROOT` and `GAME_PATH_FILE`, so `collision.py` keeps its map caches in `cache/collision` (gitignored). `tools/lobby/run.py` builds them (`tools/lobby/collision.build_movement`). Our additions (Sprint, Boosters' flight, launches, client_sync teleports, and the mover values `game_movers_174.json` misses: D.Va's mech) live in adjacent `tools/lobby/player_mover.py`.

Also from the same pin and license: `ow174/game/world.py`'s `Movement`, `write_movement`, `movement_record` and their field helpers are LizRollin's movement-state writer (replacing the snapshot's); `tools/lobby/owner_correction.py` is their `ow174/game/correction.py` with our gate and ack; `tools/lobby/test_owner_correction.py` copies the movement reader of their `tests/test_game_world.py`.

2026-11-09, same pin and license: `ow174/game/pools.py` (0033's health, armour and shield values per hero) copied byte for byte. `world.health`'s armour and shield parts are their `world.pool` layout; `tools/lobby/target.py`'s patrol walk and `Match._bot_movement` follow their `ow174/game/bots.py`. `match.py` gives each player a `PlayerMover` on `Match.world`.

2026-11-09, same pin and license: the statescript VM. Copied byte for byte: `ow174/game/script/{runtime,nodes,rulesets,coverage,driver}.py`, and their `ow174/game/statescript.py` (the VM's frame encoder; ours diverged) as `ow174/game/script/wire.py`. Local changes: one import line each in `driver.py` (`ow174.game.script.wire`) and `coverage.py` (`wire as statescript`). Also in `driver.py`, 2026-11-09: an instance variable is kept off the wire only when its own graph lists it in `m_9CEC6985` (`_kept`). Upstream merged every graph's list into one set for all instances, so 01CF's synced killer #392, which 0043, 0B8B and 01CA keep server-side, never reached the client, and the kill feed line never showed. Entity variables still use the merged set. `tools/lobby/test_vm_{driver,runtime,abilities}.py` are their `tests/test_script_{driver,runtime,abilities}.py` with the same import change, the vendor path from `practice`, and `test_vm_driver`'s `read_bindings` stand-in taking our decoder's `owner` flag. The match runs it through adjacent `tools/lobby/body_vm.py` (opt-in, `OW_BODY_VM`).

2026-11-09: `commands.py` decodes the command's view delay (`extra`) and click data (`subframe`, `click_yaw`, `click_pitch`, `view_delay()`, `aim()`), ported from LizRollin's runtime at the same pin as above. `match.py` shots leave from `Player.eye()` and test bots at `Match.view_time` (research/hitbox-drift.md items 3-4).

2026-11-09: `data/schemas_174.json` gains the lobby layout group `B9DCA497` (messages 27200-27204; 27202 is the Career Profile's stat catalogue and stats), copied from LizRollin's `data/schemas_174.json` at the same pin and license. `match.py` counts career stats per player (`Player.career`, `Player.count`; adjacent `tools/lobby/career.py` keeps them).

2026-11-09: `match.py` flies a player's projectile shots tick by tick (`Match.shots`, `_tick_shots`), after LizRollin's `combat._fly` at the same pin, against our own hit volumes.

2026-11-10, same pin and license: `data/game_stats_174.json` (the Tab board's stat lists) copied byte for byte. `world.py` gains their components 29 and 64 (64's stat GUID fields as `id`, which the live board needs, where theirs are `u64`) and the `string` field kind; `heroselect.controller_frame` gains their `presence` argument. Adjacent `tools/lobby/board.py` builds component 64 after their `stats.py` and `onfire.py`, and `match.py` sends their hero switch line (`notices.py`) and turns on each mode graph's state that lets the Tab board open (ours: research/lizrollin-runtime.md section 22).

2026-11-10: `content.game_map` sorts a control map's points by their "stage" key (it raised KeyError on every control map). `match.py` keeps an On Fire score per player (adjacent `tools/lobby/onfire.py`) and sends more modes their mode graph for the Tab board (`BOARD_MODES`).
